question: Do published Echelon cost/governance statistics (A021, A024, VAC-001, VAC-002 P3) recompute from raw records, and how many replicates would detect the claimed effects?
startRevision: cohort-based-engineering working tree as checked out 2026-11-08 (see sprint inventory/starting-revisions.tsv); praxis likewise; research-documents b372a7f (summaries only)
tools/models: python3 stdlib; reanalysis/stats.py, reanalyze.py (18 unit tests)
environment: Linux 6.18 container, 4 vCPU shared with other sprint tracks (1-min load 9-24 during runs), .NET SDK 10.0.402, warm NuGet cache
procedure: Load raw per-unit usage/verify JSON (VAC-001), per-execution score + adjudication (VAC-002 P3 S2), platform usage per session (A021, A024); recompute cost from tokens x price table 2026-10-20.1; paired percentile bootstrap (seed 20261108, 10k); exact sign / sign-flip tests; chain-level sensitivity; power by t-iteration and McNemar simulation.
verification: reanalysis/test_stats.py (18 tests pass); costs recomputed from tokens agree with recorded costs to <=4e-7 USD; acceptance proxy agrees 96/96
limitations: Bootstrap RNG differs from the original F# analysis, so CI endpoints differ in the 3rd decimal; A021/A024 have one run per arm, so variance and power for them are ESTIMATES borrowing VAC-001 variance; acceptance relies on recorded oracle/verdict outputs (oracles not re-executed).
conclusion: All 10 published numeric claims VERIFIED from raw data; VAC-001 CIs treat within-chain units as independent (3 chains); VAC-002 P3 had ~0.19-0.21 power for its realized effect and would need ~52-72 blocks.
reproduction: cd reanalysis && python3 -m unittest test_stats && python3 -I reanalyze.py /home/user/cohort-based-engineering /home/user/praxis
